chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, from Ali ibn Asbat, from al-Hasan ibn al-Jahm, from Abu al-Hasan al-Awwal (peace be upon him) who said:
Only one of the proverbs of the Prophets has remained, which is: 'If you have no shame, do whatever you wish.' He also said: 'Indeed, it applies to the Umayyad clan.'
ai.seo_question: What is the single remaining proverb of the Prophets according to the Imam?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq records this profound maxim in *Al-Khisal*, highlighting how the Umayyads epitomized the loss of *hayā'* (modesty/shame) that typically restrains human behavior, effectively reducing their rule to unbridled desire. This saying is often interpreted by Shia scholars as a diagnostic criterion for spiritual decay, where the absence of divine modesty leads to moral license, a theme deeply rooted in the prophetic tradition of using shame as a virtue.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 1-69 Muhammad ibn al-Hassan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Muhammad ibn al-Hassan al-Saffar quoted on the authority of Muhammad ibn al-Hussein ibn Abil-Khat’tab, on the authority of Ali ibn Asbat, on the authority of Al-Hassan ibn al-Jahm that Abil Hassan - the first (MGB) said,
“Only one of the proverbs from the Prophets has remained that is, ‘When you have no shame, you will do whatever you wish.’” He also said, “This applies to the Umayyad clan.”
